name: AlgMap-15.4
questiontext:
Solve the following quadratic equation by using the quadratic formula: \[ {{CT:0}} = 0. \]
Give your answer as a set \(\left(e.g. \left\{x_1 , x_2\right\} \right)\):

\({{CT:1}} \in \) [[input:ans]] [[validation:ans]]
generalfeedback:
A good method for solving any quadratic is the 'quadratic formula'. Solving a general quadratic by completing the square gives a general formula for \(x\) in terms of the coefficients of the quadratic. It is best to simply learn the quadratic formula:

For \(ax^2+bx+c = 0 \): \[ x = \frac{ -b\pm\sqrt{b^2-4ac} }{2a}. \] However it can be derived, as mentioned above, by completing the square: \[ ax^2+bx+c = 0 \] Factor out the \(x^2\) coefficient \(a\): \[ a\left(x^2+\frac{b}{a}x+\frac{c}{a}x \right) = 0. \] Complete the square: \[ a\left(\left(x+\frac{b}{2a} \right)^2-\frac{b^2}{4a^2}+\frac{c}{a}\right) = 0. \] Multiply back through by \(a\): \[ a\left(x+\frac{b}{2a} \right)^2-\frac{b^2}{4a}+c = 0. \] Rearranging gives: \[ \left(x+\frac{b}{2a}\right)^2 = \frac{b^2}{4a^2}-\frac{c}{a}. \] Simplify RHS into a single fraction: \[ \left(x+\frac{b}{2a}\right)^2 = \frac{b^2-4ac}{4a^2}. \] Square root (remember to take plus and minus): \[ \left(x+\frac{b}{2a}\right) = \pm \frac{\sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a}. \] Finally: \[ x = \frac {-b \pm \sqrt{b^2-4ac} }{2a}. \] In this exmaple: \(a = {{CT:2}}\), \(b = {{CT:3}}\), \(c = {{CT:4}}\), so subbing these into the quadratic formula gives: \[ {{CT:1}} = \frac{{{CT:5}} \pm \sqrt{{{CT:6}}-({{CT:7}})}}{{CT:8}} = {{CT:9}} \pm {{CT:10}}. \] Therefore \( {{CT:1}} = {{CT:11}}\) or \( {{CT:1}} = {{CT:12}}\) and so the solution set is: \[ {{CT:1}} \in {{CT:13}}. \]
